newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end firmer, skittish on Brazil talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end firmer, skittish on Brazil talk.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended firmer after a choppy session marked by conflicting reports on the status of an impending strike at Brazil's Paranagua port, traders said.
"The market is skittish about this rumor," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soybean values tumbled in the last hour of trade after a rumor surfaced that the Paranagua strike had been averted. But union sources told Reuters there had been no deal.
Dockworkers at the port were seeking a 21 percent pay increase and had called a strike for Wednesday.
"It has not been solved, the chance of a strike is 90 percent," Ana Lucia Ferrera, chief negotiator for the port operators union SINDOP, told Reuters.
The port authority said a strike would not affect soybean loading at the port because much of the operations are automated.
"The loading of grains is made by conveyor belts, it is all automated," a port spokeswoman said. "With five people you can operate the export terminal."
Soybeans ended 5-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with March up 1-1/2 at $8.06-1/2.

Bears pointed to news Brazil's soybean crop was eight percent harvested as of February 27, a record pace, according to independent consultants Safras e Mercado. The harvest was four percent complete at the same time last year.
Hedge selling was noted as farmer sales picked up, floor sources said. Cargill Inc sold 0.5 million bushels March, 1.5 million May and one million November.
Farmers Commodities Corp sold one million May and Term Commodities sold 1.5 million May, traders said.

In options trade, Cargill Inc reportedly sold 1,300 May $8.00 puts at 20-1/4 to 20-1/2 cents. Produce Grain reportedly bought 400 May $7.75 puts and sold 400 May $7.50 puts at six cents, traders said. Smith Barney bought 600 May $7.75 calls.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 67,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 69,381 contracts.
